newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese prosecutor says MP wants rebellion.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese prosecutor says MP wants rebellion.

text.p: A Beirut prosecutor has accused opposition member of parliament Najah Wakim of advocating armed rebellion and slandering Lebanese President Elias Hrawi.

The rebellion charge carries up to 10 years imprisonment while slander offences carry up to three years. A senior judicial source said Wakim would be summoned for questioning by Beirut magistrate Fouad Geagea on Tuesday.

The senior official, who asked not to be identified, said on Monday the charges filed by prosecutor Jihad al-Wadi against Wakim included "calling for armed civil disobedience, humiliating the judiciary and slandering the president".
Firebrand Wakim defended himself at a news conference at his Beirut home: "I did not call for an armed rebellion. I called for confronting the authorities with all possible peaceful means."
After a meeting with parliamentary speaker Nabih Berri, Wakim told reporters that the charges against him were unfounded and denied that he had slandered the president.
Beirut newspapers had quoted Wakim as saying in the eastern town of Baalbek on Sunday: "We are making the necessary arrangements to expand civil disobedience to cover the whole of Lebanon."

He spoke at a rally called by Sheikh Sobhi al-Tufaili, former secretary general of the Moslem group Hizbollah, who last month declared a civil disobedience campaign in the impoverished Baalbek-Hermel region.

On July 4, Tufaili urged residents to refuse to pay utility bills and taxes to pressure the government to tackle poverty in the area, which is suffering economically from a crackdown on illegal drug crops.
Wakim, 53-year-old Greek Orthodox politician, is one of the liveliest critics of Lebanon's political establishment. He was re-elected for a four-year term in last year's parliamentary elections.
